title: The two-term resolution of the finite coefficient sheaves
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite with uniformizer $\pi_E$ and $n\geq1$. For every scheme $X$
the sequence of $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-module sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$

$$
0\to\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \pi_E^n\ }\mathcal O_{E,X}\to(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\to0
$$

is exact. Consequently, for $K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$,
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ is
isomorphic to the cone of $\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$, naturally in $K$, and for
$1\leq m\leq n$ there are triangles
$K_m\xrightarrow{\pi_E^{n}}K_{n+m}\to K_n\to$, in particular
$K_1\to K_{n+1}\to K_n\to$.

proof.text: Let A be the recorded integer subring and pi its recorded uniformizer. The nonzero maximal ideal generated by pi implies pi is nonzero. Multiplication by pi^n is injective for every n, including n=0. Transport the spectral-norm neighbourhood basis to the absolute-value topology using equality of their metrics. The coset-basis theorem makes reduction modulo pi^(n+1) locally constant, so the quotient topology is discrete; at n=0 the quotient is a singleton. Use continuous_uniformizer_division for continuous division on the image of pi^n.

source.place: On the point: topology, nonzero uniformizer, and continuous division

proof.text: Construct the internal-module endomorphism d by pointwise multiplication by pi and construct r_n from the actual continuous quotient ring map. Check linearity after the sheaf tensor comparison on pure tensors. Induction computes d^n sectionwise as multiplication by pi^n, and quotient membership proves d^n followed by r_n is zero. For every profinite S, multiplication is injective by cancellation. A section in the kernel has a continuous quotient by continuous_uniformizer_division. A section of the discrete quotient lifts by composition with a set-theoretic section of A onto A/(pi^n); every map from this discrete quotient is continuous. This includes the empty profinite set and n=0. Sectionwise kernel forks form a kernel in the presheaf category, and the faithful sheaf inclusion reflects this kernel and epimorphisms. The exact faithful internal-module forgetful functor then reflects short exactness.

source.place: On the point: the three sectionwise exactness checks

proof.text: The first factor of upperStarFromPoint is sheafified left Kan extension along the finite-limit-preserving profinite test-object functor. The adopted source theorem preservesFiniteLimits_op_lan_of_flat, together with AB5 for abelian groups and left-exact sheafification, proves its finite-limit preservation. Its adjunction and the scheme inverse-image adjunction give finite-colimit preservation; the existing scheme inverse-image instances give finite-limit preservation for the other factor. The mapMod functor transports both properties, hence preserves the exact point sequences. Its regular module is the tensor unit through the unchanged regularPullbackIso. For the cone comparison transport the full short complex through regularPullbackIso by ShortComplex.isoMk; the reduction map out of the unit is its inverse followed by the pulled-back reduction. This avoids unfolding equality proofs between the full internal-module records.

source.place: On X: exact inverse image and transported coefficient actions

proof.text: Use the adopted proved DerivedCategory.reductionIso from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Monoidal.TensorMappingCone. Its proof identifies the cone of the degree-zero map of the tensor unit with the quotient in degree zero; this is the same two-term rank-one resolution as in the unit proof. The cone is K-flat because the tensor unit is K-flat and K-flat objects form a triangulated subcategory. Thus its tensor comparison is an isomorphism for every possibly unbounded complex; no change to the unit resolution route is made. To apply its linear formulation, give a private copy of End(unit) its commutative ring structure by naturality of the unit action. Send it to the categorical center, obtaining a linear monoidal action. Coherence and the braiding identify right and left unit actions.

source.place: On X: the augmented rank-one free resolution is K-flat

proof.text: Identify the scalar natural transformation on complexes with the file's scalarOnComplex degree by degree. For the scalar transformation itself, reductionIso_hom_naturality assembles its component isomorphisms into a natural isomorphism between Q followed by the reduction functor and the fixed mapping-cone functor. Transport this along the equality of natural transformations. This verifies exactly the standard cone maps already specified in coneFunctor, rather than choosing cones separately.

For all m,n use the cokernel-of-composition snake input in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.DiagramLemmas.KernelCokernelComp with f=d^m and g=d^n. Its last three cokernels form an exact sequence, its last arrow is epic, and its first arrow is monic because ker(g)=0. The short exact point resolutions identify these cokernels canonically with B_m, B_(n+m), B_n. Conjugating the canonical cokernel maps by these identifications gives i and q. The cokernel equations prove r_m followed by i equals d^n followed by r_(n+m), and r_(n+m) followed by q equals r_n. Thus these are exactly the normalized quotient-power maps of the blueprint; the argument also works when an exponent is zero.

source.place: Triangles: normalized quotient-power maps and short exactness

proof.text: Pull back this short exact sequence and place it in degree zero. DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES_distinguished gives its distinguished triangle. The adopted triangulated tensorLeft K functor preserves the triangle for every unbounded K. The first two mapped arrows are definitionally reductionMap i and reductionMap q, and the third arrow supplies the requested connecting morphism. Restricting to the stated positive exponents and m <= n proves the displayed clause.

source.place: Triangles: the short-exact-sequence triangle and derived tensor
